items.title: The true price of Intelligence: an economic study by Signal65
items.summary: As AI workloads move from lab to production, the true cost of intelligence has become one of the most consequential decisions platform leaders face. This session presents Signal65's in-depth economic study of training and inference costs across CoreWeave and leading hyperscalers covering cloud economics, performance benchmarks, and multi-year TCO impact. The analysis goes beyond compute pricing to expose the hidden costs that compound at scale, and how infrastructure economics translate directly into token costs at production volume. Attendees will leave with a clear framework for evaluating fully-loaded economics across the complete training-to-inference lifecycle.

items.title: Automating document work with Long-Horizon AI Agents at LlamaIndex
items.summary: ~90% of enterprise data is unstructured, and a lot of that lives in the form of documents - PDFs, pptx, docx, etc. - powering a majority of enterprise knowledge work. AI agents have the potential to simultaneously better make sense of docs and also automate human workflows over them. Existing document AI use cases have either been long-running but constrained (e.g. a batch invoice processing through RPA), or non-deterministic but short-horizon (e.g. ChatGPT deep research over a collection of existing files). Going forward there's a huge opportunity to build long-running agents that can understand, reason over, and edit documents at scale. In this session, we'll walk through core advances in document OCR and agent orchestration that have given rise to initial use cases around doc extraction workflows and general-purpose chatbots (and share real-world customer use cases). We will then articulate some of the remaining gaps needed to achieve "long-running" document work automation.

items.title: Empowering Intelligence: democratizing data access and driving smarter decisions at Nasdaq
items.summary: See how one of the world's most data-intensive technology companies is putting AI-ready capabilities into the hands of its clients, not just a specialized few. Nasdaq will share how it's rethinking the path from raw market and operational data to decisions clients can act on in real time. You'll hear where self-service access unlocks speed, where governance and compliance still have to hold the line, and how CoreWeave's infrastructure factors into scaling that work. You'll also hear concrete examples of efficiency gains from reducing the friction between data and the people who need it — and what it took organizationally, not just technically, to get there. Walk away with a practical view of how a highly regulated, high-stakes environment is balancing broader data democratization with the resilience its business depends on.

items.title: Beyond the Harness: How LiquidAI Is solving the real frontier problems in on-device Agents
items.summary: Most agent harness architectures look the same whether they run in the cloud or on a device, until you actually try to ship one on a phone, a car, or a laptop. That's where three problems show up that don't have good answers yet: Routing intelligently between edge and cloud, building an edge-sized model capable enough to be the agent's main"brain" (with planning, memory, and execution), and acting on interfaces with no API or MCP tool to call. Jeffrey Li, COO of Liquid AI, walks through how Liquid is tackling each of these in production, drawing on how routing decisions actually play out in real deployments. You'll also learn how Liquid trained device-native foundation models with CoreWeave, models designed from the outset for constrained, on-device environments rather than compressed down after the fact, and how they’re thinking about governance, control, and observability as agents increasingly execute across both edge and cloud.

items.title: Benchmark LLMs on your own transcripts with Voice Standard Bench
items.summary: General LLM leaderboards score coding, math and chat. None of them score what a model does with a real transcript: the filler words, missing punctuation and misheard names that come out of Speech-to-Text. Voice Standard Bench does. In this video we clone it, point it at a folder of our own audio, and get back a leaderboard for those transcripts. Voice Standard Bench scores every model on AssemblyAI's LLM Gateway, 50+ today, on the tasks voice products hand to an LLM: summarization, information extraction, text correction and dictation cleanup. Each task runs at four transcript lengths, from a 30-second voicemail to an hour-long meeting. Every model gets the same transcripts and the same prompt. Two judge models score each answer against a fixed rubric, and the run logs every format failure, refusal and timeout. Quality, response time and cost per hour of audio are reported side by side. The published results are the starting point.
